articles.title: SRVC Bandwar Volleyball: The Annual Clash at SNK Ground
articles.subtitle: Dust, sweat, and village pride at Bandwar's premier volleyball tournament
articles.summary: The SRVC Bandwar Volleyball Tournament is one of the most anticipated sporting events in the village. Held annually on the cemented court of S.N.K. High School, right next to the Maharshi Gautam Durga Mandir, the tournament brings together local teams for a fierce but friendly battle. It is a true reflection of the village's love for the game, where the cheers of the crowd echo against the school walls and the temple bells.

content.heading: The Venue: A Historic Ground
content.text: The tournament is not played on any modern indoor court; it takes place on a raw, cemented court laid out on the open grounds of S.N.K. High School. Established in 1942, this ground has been the beating heart of Bandwar's sporting culture for decades. The court itself, bordered by lush green grass, has witnessed generations of young men diving and sweating for every point. What makes this venue even more special is its surroundings—the pink walls of the school building, the towering telecom mast in the distance, and the Maharshi Gautam Durga Mandir standing right next door, adding a sense of local pride and spiritual blessing to every match.

content.heading: SRVC and the Spirit of the Game
content.text: Organised by the local youth and sports enthusiasts under the SRVC Bandwar banner, the tournament is a labour of love. There is no corporate sponsorship, no massive prize money, and no professional referees. It is organised purely for the love of the game. Teams from different tolas of Bandwar and neighboring villages register to compete. As seen in the photographs, the sidelines are often dotted with bicycles—the primary mode of transport for these young athletes who ride down from their fields and homes to play. The matches are fast, the spikes are aggressive, and the crowd cheers for every single serve.

content.heading: Evenings at the SNK Ground
content.text: The true magic of the SRVC tournament unfolds in the late afternoon. As the sun begins to set, casting long, golden shadows across the green grass and the concrete court, the energy on the ground reaches its peak. Players in bright jerseys—reds, blues, and yellows—leap high against the backdrop of the sky. The air fills with the sound of the whistle, the thud of the ball hitting the hard surface, and the loud shouts of 'Out!' and 'Mine!'. Elders sit on the grass to discuss techniques, women cheer from the sidelines, and children run to fetch the ball when it goes out of bounds. The atmosphere is electric, a perfect blend of sportsmanship and rural community life.

content.heading: More Than Just a Game
content.text: For the youth of Bandwar, this tournament is a platform to showcase their talent and gain respect. Several local players have honed their skills on this very court and gone on to represent the block or district level. But more importantly, the SRVC tournament is a time of unity. It bridges social gaps, brings old rivalries to the court, and ends with a mutual respect for the game. It is a festival of sports that sits perfectly alongside the village's other grand traditions like the [[janmashtami-mela-bandwar-bihar|Janmashtami Mela]] and the [[shahid-rajesh-memorial-cricket-tournament-bandwar|Shahid Rajesh Memorial Cricket Tournament]].

faqs.q: Where is the SRVC Volleyball Tournament held?
faqs.a: The tournament is held on the cemented court at the ground of S.N.K. High School in Bandwar. The ground is located right next to the Maharshi Gautam Durga Mandir.

faqs.q: Who organises the volleyball tournament in Bandwar?
faqs.a: It is organised by SRVC Bandwar, a local sports group comprising the village youth who manage the teams, the ground, and the schedule of the matches.

faqs.q: Can teams from other villages participate?
faqs.a: Yes, while it is a local village tournament, it often draws teams from neighboring villages who come to compete at the SNK ground.
